additions.site_name: Envision Ulanqab Zero-Carbon AI Computing Industrial Park (Yiwutang)
additions.name: Envision Ulanqab Zero-Carbon AI Computing Industrial Park — Phase 1

status.summary: On 24 October 2026 CSCEC reported that Phase 1 of the Envision Ulanqab Zero-Carbon AI Computing Industrial Park (远景乌兰察布零碳人工智能算力产业园（一期）项目) in the Chahar High-Tech Development Zone, built by its subsidiary China Construction Third Engineering Bureau, is advancing and currently in its construction-finishing stage, with the remaining finishing and commissioning work still to be completed. Completion, commissioning completion and operation are not established; no capacity is asserted. Phase 2 (planned) and the separately reported Phase 3 are not part of this project.

locator.precision: EIA centre point of the Phase 1 park's own 220 kV substation, which the report places inside the Phase 1 plant area on its north side, just south of the east-west road (Pingzan Street). Locates the Phase 1 park through on-campus support infrastructure; not a data-centre building footprint, parcel centroid, entrance or construction extent. On the report's map the park extends up to about 600 m south and 400 m east of the point.
locator.identity_review: The report form published by the Inner Mongolia Department of Ecology and Environment on 10 February 2026 (approval 内环表〔2026〕15号) is for the substation supporting 远景乌兰察布零碳人工智能算力产业园项目一期, built by Envision (Ulanqab) Technology Development Co., Ltd. under the Phase 1 filing code 2501-150982-89-04-953605, and places it inside the Phase 1 plant area at Yiwutang Industrial Park, Chahar High-Tech Zone, on the plant's north side with Xiaobei Village 123 m east. CSCEC's 24 October 2026 item names the same project (远景乌兰察布零碳人工智能算力产业园（一期）项目) in the Chahar High-Tech Zone. The printed centre (113°14′54.505″E, 40°56′55.632″N) is the centroid of the printed enclosure corners (0.07 m; area 7,860 m2 against the reported 7,843 m2) and is drawn at those values on the report's graticuled figure 4, whose graticule agrees with an independent Esri WGS84 export within about 10 m at a road junction and a tree-line junction. Read as WGS84 the enclosure falls south of the road and east of the north-south main road with Xiaobei Village to its east, as in the report; the GCJ-02 reading would put it about 620 m west-south-west, west of the main road. Details: sources/research-countries-2026-10-26-cn-nm-nx-gs-p3-envision-ulanqab-phase1-geometry-facts.json.
locator.uncertainty_reason: No datum or positional accuracy is stated. The CGCS2000/WGS84 reading is supported by the report's internally consistent enclosure corners and by agreement of its figure-4 graticule with independent Esri imagery within about 10 m at two ground features (manual pixel picks against imagery of unstated accuracy and date). The point marks the planned on-campus substation, not the Phase 1 data-centre buildings, which may lie several hundred metres south or east. Decimal places are transcription precision, not accuracy.

No queue fragment adds a record within 2 km, and no other fragment has claimed Envision. Holds: the sixty-fourth bounded hold 'Envision Ulanqab zero-carbon AI industrial park Phase 1' (status lead from the same CSCEC item, locator unresolved) and the Envision Phase 1 entry in the cn-north-p1 Ulanqab hold (ancillary 220 kV approval only) are resolved here by the Phase 1 substation EIA and the in-window CSCEC record. additions.successor_review: Re-checked 26 October 2026: CSCEC's 24 October item is the newest dated record found for Phase 1. The Inner Mongolia Department of Ecology and Environment approval-result lists (newest 8 October 2026) show no completion-acceptance or later item for the Phase 1 substation or park; Envision's website is a JavaScript application with no server-rendered news; the Ulanqab municipal hosts (www.wulanchabu.gov.cn, sthjj/zrzyj.wulanchabu.gov.cn) failed to connect and were not retried. An Envision release of 6 August 2026 reported a formal opening of its 'Galaxy' base at Ulanqab and a 20 August interview said Phase 1 was about to be handed over; neither ties the Galaxy base to this park or establishes completion or operation of Phase 1, and CSCEC's later report still describes finishing and commissioning work. Keep under construction as of 24 October 2026.

additions.site_name: CIDC Jing-Meng Green Computing Industrial Park (Ulanqab D-Zone)
additions.name: CIDC Jing-Meng Green Computing Industrial Park — D-Zone Development

status.summary: On 13 October 2026 Beijing Urban Construction Group, whose No.2 Company builds CIDC's Ulanqab cluster, reported that the Jing-Meng Green Computing Industrial Park D-zone (530 mu; construction started March 2025) is racing toward its completion and handover target, with interiors and equipment installed as prefabricated modular cabins after the main structure. Completion, handover and operation are not established; the cluster-wide 800 MW IT figure is not attributed to the D-zone. The operating zones A-C base is the separate existing Atlas site.

locator.precision: EIA centre point of the Jing-Meng Phase 2 220 kV substation, which the report places inside the Phase 2 project area at its east edge (D9 compute centre to the west, open land to the east). Locates the D-zone park through on-campus support infrastructure; not a data-centre building footprint, parcel centroid, entrance or construction extent. The D-zone buildings extend up to roughly 500-600 m west and south-west of the point.
locator.identity_review: The report form published by the Inner Mongolia Department of Ecology and Environment on 16 October 2025 (approval 内环表〔2025〕281号) is for the 220 kV substation of 中金数据京蒙绿色算力产业园二期项目, built by CIDC (Ulanqab) Data Technology Co., Ltd., and places it inside the Phase 2 project area of the Jing-Meng Green Computing Industrial Park in Bayin Industrial Park, Chahar High-Tech Zone; its figure 4 shows the Phase 1 area in the south-west of the park outline and the substation in the north-east. BUCG's 13 October 2026 item names the same park's D-zone (京蒙绿色算力产业园D区, 530 mu, started March 2025, the month the Phase 2 project EIA was approved) as the extension east of CIDC's zones A-C base; the report's Phase 2 area alone is 250,296 m2 (about 375 mu), and with the Phase 1 area shown on its figure 4 the park is consistent with the 530-mu D-zone. Printed 113°19′40.937″E, 40°59′21.135″N, transcribed arithmetically. Read as WGS84 the point falls at the north-east corner of the new building block east of the road bounding the zones A-C base, with open land east and Duanjia Village about 320 m east, as the report says (278 m from the station wall); the GCJ-02 reading would put it about 634 m west-south-west in the road corridor. Details: sources/research-countries-2026-10-26-cn-nm-nx-gs-p3-cidc-jingmeng-d-zone-geometry-facts.json.
locator.uncertainty_reason: No datum or positional accuracy is stated, and the report prints no corner coordinates or graticule. The WGS84 reading rests on qualitative agreement with the report's neighbour statements, its Google Earth surroundings figure and an independent Esri export of unstated accuracy and date. The point marks the planned on-campus substation at the park's east edge, not the D-zone data-centre buildings, which extend several hundred metres west and south-west. Decimal places are transcription precision, not accuracy.

additions.site_name: China Telecom Cloud Computing Inner Mongolia Information Park (Horinger)
additions.name: China Telecom Cloud Computing Inner Mongolia Information Park — existing data-centre operations

status.summary: On 15 September 2026 the Horinger New Area approvals and government-services bureau stated that the China Telecom Cloud Computing Inner Mongolia Information Park recovers data-centre waste heat through water-source heat pumps, with a single machine building able to heat about 360,000 m2 of homes, which describes the park's data-centre buildings as currently operating. The record covers the park's existing operations as a whole; no opening date, capacity, rack count or building list is asserted, area-wide compute figures are not transferred, and the park's expansion works and its new third 220 kV substation are not described as complete.

locator.precision: EIA centre point of the park's new (third) 220 kV substation, which the report places inside the information park's land red line at the south-east corner of its B-zone plot on the east section of Yunzhan Road. Locates the park through on-campus power infrastructure at its south side; not an operating data-centre building, entrance or parcel centroid. The park's data-centre buildings extend up to roughly 800 m west-north-west and 700 m north of the point.
locator.identity_review: The report form published by the Inner Mongolia Department of Ecology and Environment on 7 June 2026 (approval 内环表〔2026〕94号) is for the 220 kV substation that China Telecom Corporation Limited Cloud Computing Inner Mongolia Branch is building for the China Telecom Cloud Computing Inner Mongolia Information Park, which design documents call the park's third 220 kV substation. It places the station inside the park plant area and within the park's land red line (B-zone plot, south-east corner; east section of Yunzhan Road, Shengle Modern Service Industry Cluster) and attaches the park's 2013 land-use planning permit (948,218 m2 = 1,422.3 mu). The 15 September 2026 status record names the same park. Printed N40°32'15.394", E111°49'51.772", transcribed arithmetically; the substation symbol on the report's 5-arc-second graticuled figure sits within about 3 m of that value, and that graticule agrees with an independent Esri WGS84 export within about 6 m at a road intersection and at the park's circular plaza. Read as WGS84 the point falls in the southern part of the road-bounded data-centre compound; the GCJ-02 reading would put it about 580 m west-south-west, outside the park. Details: sources/research-countries-2026-10-26-cn-nm-nx-gs-p3-china-telecom-inner-mongolia-information-park-geometry-facts.json.
locator.uncertainty_reason: No datum or positional accuracy is stated. The CGCS2000/WGS84 reading is supported by the report's own graticuled figure and its agreement with independent Esri imagery within about 6 m at two ground features (manual pixel picks against imagery of unstated accuracy and date). The point marks a planned on-campus substation at the park's south side, several hundred metres from most data-centre buildings. Decimal places are transcription precision, not accuracy.
